chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal,

He said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr), and he said: 'It is obligatory upon the young and the old, the free and the slave, for every person a sa' of wheat, or a sa' of dates, or a sa' of raisins.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.صَاعٌ: A traditional unit of volume measurement used for Zakat al-Fitr

ai.seo_question: What is the amount and type of food required for Zakat al-Fitr in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the universality of Zakat al-Fitr, emphasizing its obligation on every individual regardless of age, freedom, or status, thereby reinforcing its role as a purifying act for the fasting person. The specification of staple foods like wheat, dates, and raisins reflects the dietary norms of Medina and aligns with the Prophetic tradition of providing sustenance to the poor. This ruling underscores the social welfare dimension of Zakat, ensuring that the needy can celebrate Eid with dignity.
